texts.preamble: Theerthesh Alias Threethesh vs Shekhar on 28 January, 2026 Kabc020201232023 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: this the 28th day of January 2026 Present: Dhanesh Mugali B.Com., LL.B.,(Spl.) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact, Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Mvc No.4543/2023
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident. Brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under 2. That on 1.2.2022 at about 7.00 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a RX Yamaha motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-11-K- 9130 the same was ridden by his friend by name Theerthesh on Hirisave-Shravanabelagola road, when they reached splendor motor cycle bearing No.KA13- ES-1636 ridden by its rider with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding. Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries. 3. It is further stated that, immediately he was shifted to General Hospital, Hirisave for first aid, then he was shifted to Punya hospital, Channarayapatna for further treatment, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation, treatment, medicines, conveyance etc., 4. It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and working as X-ray technician at Punya Hospital, Channarayapatna and also doing agriculture and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to do his work as earlier. 5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to negligent act of rider of Splendor motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-13-ES-1636. Hence the Hirisave Police have filed charge sheet against rider of said vehicle in Cr.No17/2022. As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation. 6. After service of summons, respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court, remained absent, hence placed exparte. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement. 7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of Hyundai Car bearing registration No.KA-13-ES-1636 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy. It is contended that, the rider of offending vehicle had no valid and effective riding licence to ride the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy. It is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-11-K- 9130. Further Theerthesh Alias Threethesh vs Shekhar on 28 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139049892/ 2 contended that rider and the pillion rider were not wearing the safety head gear at the time of accident. Further stated that there is delay in lodging the complaint. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner. Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant. With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P8. 10. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW1 & RW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R6. Further examined ASI of Hirisave Police Station as RW3. 11.
